To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mercury stimulates glucocorticoid‐receptor association with heat shock proteins.

1) mercury stimulates association of heat shock proteins HSP90 and HSP70 with the GR, 2) mercury does not affect the total amounts of HSP90 and/or HSP70 in the cytosol, 3) the effect of mercury on GR/HSP association does not depend on the dose of mercury administered to rats, and 4) mercury stimulates association with HSP90 and 70 in the absence of GR ligand.
the mercury administration stimulates the association of Hsp90 or/and Hsp70 with the rat liver glucocoricosteroid receptor, rendering hepatic cytosolic levels of these heat shock proteins unaltered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the action of mercury on the liver glucocorticoids receptor.
the mechanisms controlling association of glucocorticoid receptors with Hsp90, Hsp70 and other proteins.
the mechanisms regulating the association of the glucocorticod receptor with heat shock proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mercury stimulates association between the glucocorticoids receptor and heat shock proteins, but the mechanism of this action remains unknown.
the mercury‐induced alterations in the association of Hsp90, Hsp70 and GR are a consequence of the mercury‐inducible changes in the levels of the heat shock proteins.

the mercury‐induced increase in the association between the GR and the Hsps is not a direct effect of mercury on the Hsps, but rather an effect of mercury on a regulatory process controlling the assembly of these heterocomplexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mercury affects the assembly of the glucocorticoids receptor heterocomplex with the two heat shock protein HSP90 and HSP70.
mercury affects the assembly of the glucocorticoids receptor heterocomplex.
mercury stimulates the association of the glucocorticiod receptor with heat shock proteins, rendering the cytoplasmic level of these proteins unchanged.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mercury affects the assembly of GR‐Hsp complexes, which may have implications in the mechanism of GR‐induced hepatotoxicity.
mercury stimulates the association of the glucocorticid receptor with heat shock proteins.
mercury stimulates GR association with Hsp70 and Hsp90.
